data_analyst.analysis_summary: The evidence shows that the facility's order was placed on time and delivered as expected, ruling out a late order (H1). The facility's fill rate (70.1%) is markedly lower than the county average (89.6%), indicating a strong under‑supply signal (H2). There are no payment arrears or county‑wide fill drops linked to financing issues (H3). Consumption actually fell 25% below the three‑month average, so demand surge is not supported (H4). Stock records reconcile and the reported four‑day stockout is plausible, providing no record‑error signal (H5). However, the facility recorded 146 units of wastage this month versus a three‑month average of zero, exceeding both the 2× historical threshold and 10% of consumption, which is a strong expiry‑related waste signal (H6). No public web notice of a national disruption was found, so the national disruption hypothesis lacks support (H7).

H1.reasoning: Order placed on 2026-02-09 before the 2026-02-10 cutoff; delivery occurred in the expected month with no slip (orders#2177).

H2.reasoning: Facility fill rate 0.7013 is substantially below the county average 0.8963 (relative shortfall 0.1951), flagged as underfill (orders#2177).

H3.reasoning: No arrears recorded (amount owed 0 KES) and county fill actually rose from 0.8963 to 0.9248; no payment‑related drop observed.

H4.reasoning: Consumption this month (223) is 25.5% lower than the three‑month average (299.33); no surge detected (stock#2178).

H5.reasoning: Closing balances match, stock identity holds, and reported stockout days are plausible; no record error (stock#2178).

H6.reasoning: Wastage this month (146) far exceeds the three‑month average (0) and is >10% of consumption (22.3), meeting the expiry‑wastage criteria (stock#2178).

H7.reasoning: Although county fill changed slightly, no public web notice of a national disruption was found.

data_limitations: Analysis is limited to a single month (2026-03) and may not capture longer‑term trends.
Wastage classification assumes expiry; other causes (e.g., damage, mis‑use) are not distinguished.
Web‑notice search may miss informal or non‑indexed announcements of national disruptions.
Fill‑rate calculations rely on reported deliveries; unrecorded informal supplies could affect accuracy.

theories.mechanism: If the facility submits its order after the monthly cutoff, the supplier schedules the shipment for the next cycle, creating a gap between consumption and receipt that can produce a stockout.

Other facilities with on‑time orders do not experience a stockout in the same period

theories.title: Supplier delivered less than requested

predictions: Facility fill‑rate remains markedly below the county average

theories.mechanism: When the county owes ≥30 M KES, the supplier may withhold or reduce shipments county‑wide, limiting the quantity delivered to each facility and causing stockouts.
evidence_needed: Financial records confirming arrears of ≥30 M KES at the county level

predictions: Multiple facilities in the same county report stockouts in the same month

theories.title: Unexpected demand spike exhausted stock
theories.mechanism: A consumption increase >25 % above the three‑month average depletes inventory faster than forecasted, leaving no stock before the next delivery.
evidence_needed: Monthly consumption data showing >25 % rise over the prior three‑month average

predictions: Stockout coincides with the period of highest daily issue rates

theories.title: Stockout days misrecorded due to data entry error
theories.mechanism: Incorrect entry in the stock card or electronic system could flag a stockout when physical stock was actually available, inflating the apparent shortage.
evidence_needed: Audit of the stock card for the March 2026 period
Physical inventory verification matching on‑hand balances with recorded values
Comparison of reported stockout days with timestamps of issue transactions
disconfirming_evidence: Physical count confirms zero stock for the reported days

No discrepancies found during an independent audit
predictions: Reconciliation reveals mismatched dates between stockout flag and actual issue activity
Corrected records show fewer or no stockout days after audit
Other facilities using the same reporting system exhibit similar error patterns

theories.title: Large expiry or damage waste depleted usable stock
theories.mechanism: A substantial write‑off of 146 units as wastage (expiry, damage, or mis‑use) removed a significant portion of the usable inventory, leaving insufficient stock to meet demand.
evidence_needed: Wastage log detailing batch numbers, expiry dates, and reason codes for the 146 units
Comparison of monthly wastage trends showing this month as an outlier
Physical verification that the expired/damaged units were removed from usable stock
disconfirming_evidence: Wastage classified under reasons unrelated to expiry (e.g., administrative adjustment)
Expired units were already excluded from the usable balance before the month began

predictions: Usable stock balance drops sharply in the inventory ledger immediately after the wastage entry
Future orders increase to compensate for the loss
Facility reports higher proportion of expired stock in subsequent quality audits

theories.title: National supply chain disruption limited deliveries
theories.mechanism: A country‑wide issue such as a tender failure, logistics breakdown, or regulatory notice curtails the flow of commodities, reducing deliveries to all counties and causing localized stockouts.
evidence_needed: Public notices, tender cancellation documents, or ministry communications about a supply disruption in early 2026

disconfirming_evidence: No national announcements or media reports of a disruption during the period

Logistics partners report normal operations
predictions: Concurrent stockouts of oxytocin (and possibly other commodities) reported in several facilities across the country
